# A disconnected actual fixed-rate group and the common-lift obstruction

This is an explicit geometric inverse-volume rate example. It strengthens
the symmetric example in
geometric-rate-group-kernel-and-exact-phase-compensation-rate-geometry.md.
All affine planes belong to ONE limiting gradient group. Each individual
cell has the residual positive-concave density proved in the companion
note, but their group sum has disconnected support and arbitrarily small
halfspace depth at its centroid. It is not the marginal of uniform
volume on any one convex body.

No assertion is made that this geometry satisfies the extra variational
stationarity equations of a selected deepest-point minimization.
In fact the attained sampled canonical PL representative has at most
ONE source plane per integer source base. Here n=0 has only one source
base but (2) uses two planes, so this example is NOT in that narrower
canonical class. It obstructs a theorem based solely on generic PL
geometry, rate kernels, and per-cell positive concavity. It does not
exclude additional control from distinct source-base labels and their
actual touching/optimality conditions.

## 1. Exact convex bodies and affine rates

Use n=0,d=3, with coordinates (s,x,y), and put t=x+y. Set

    H(s)=max(2-s,1+s),              0<=s<=1,
    a=1/10,    b=1/100,
    ell(s)=841/445+(9/89)s,
    A(s)=max(H(s),ell(s)).

The affine function ell is the chord between (a,2-a) and (1-b,2-b).
Its slope 9/89 lies strictly between -1 and 1. Hence

    E={s:A(s)=H(s)}=[0,1/10] union [99/100,1].             (1)

For integers j>=3 and a fixed rho>0 put

    delta_j=1/j,  eta_j=exp(-j),  lambda_j=rho/j,

    K_j={0<=s<=1, x,y>=0, delta_j A(s)<=x+y<=1},

    L_j(s,x,y)=t-delta_j H(s)+eta_j
       =min(t-delta_j(2-s)+eta_j,
            t-delta_j(1+s)+eta_j).                         (2)

These are compact full-dimensional convex polytopes and positive
piecewise-affine concave functions. Since A>=H, L_j>=eta_j on K_j.
Both active affine planes converge, with their gradients, to the SAME
plane L=t. The bodies converge in Hausdorff distance to

    K=[0,1] x {x,y>=0:x+y<=1},   M=|K|=1/2.               (3)

The common zero face is

    F={(s,0,0):0<=s<=1},

of dimension 1=d-2. Reciprocal integrability holds:

    integral_K 1/(x+y) d(s,x,y)=1.

Indeed (x,y)=(vt,(1-v)t), 0<=v<=1, has Jacobian t, and
0<=t<=1. The prelimit volumes satisfy

    M_j=|K_j|=(1/2) integral_0^1 [1-delta_j^2 A(s)^2]ds
       ->1/2.                                             (4)

All bodies lie in one fixed compact set, A<=2, and M_j are bounded
uniformly away from zero.

## 2. The exact positive-rate inverse law

Define

    r_j=lambda_j(-log L_j)_+,
    dI_j=1_(K_j) d(s,x,y)/(M_j L_j).

For every fixed rate 0<r<rho the level L_j=exp(-rj/rho) has

    t_j(s,r)=delta_j H(s)-eta_j+exp(-rj/rho).               (5)

It is in K_j precisely when

    delta_j[A(s)-H(s)]<=exp(-rj/rho)-eta_j,
    t_j(s,r)<=1.                                         (6)

The second condition holds for all sufficiently large j. The first
condition tends pointwise to 1_E(s), apart from endpoints, which do not
affect any density below. On E it holds for every r<rho; outside E it
eventually fails.

In the (s,t,v) coordinates, d(s,x,y)=t ds dt dv. Along a rate level,
|dt/dr|=L_j/lambda_j, so the exact positive-rate slice measure is

    [t_j(s,r)/(M_j lambda_j)] 1_(condition (6)) ds dv,      (7)

pushed to (s,v t_j,(1-v)t_j). Its physical points converge to (s,0,0),
and, for each fixed r in (0,rho),

    t_j(s,r)/(M_j lambda_j) -> 2H(s)/rho

uniformly in s before multiplying by the indicator. The densities are
uniformly bounded for each such r. Dominated convergence therefore
gives the finite weak limit

    gamma_G(r,ds)=(2/rho)H(s)1_E(s)ds,    0<r<rho.          (8)

For r>rho the slice is empty because exp(-rj/rho)<eta_j.
The positive-rate law has no atom at rho. The canonical group density
has the displayed value below rho and zero above it.

Formula (7) also agrees exactly with ordinary affine-slice coarea.
On the first or second active cell, its N=2 surface element is
t_j sqrt(2+delta_j^2)ds dv, while the active continuous gradient has
norm sqrt(2+delta_j^2). Dividing by M_j lambda_j times this gradient
norm gives (7). Thus this is the actual common-normalized slice law,
not an arbitrarily prescribed density.

The first global active cell has positive-rate limit supported on
[0,1/10] with affine density proportional to 2-s. The other has limit
supported on [99/100,1] with affine density proportional to 1+s.
Each has q=1, N=2, and residual exponent N-q=1, exactly as predicted
by the individual-component theorem.

## 3. The group centroid has a certified small cap

Normalization and the constant 2/rho cancel when computing the centroid
and cap fractions. For the measure H(s)1_E(s)ds the two interval masses
are

    m_left=39/200,       m_right=399/20000,
    m_total=4299/20000.

Their first moments are

    u_left=29/3000,      u_right=59551/3000000,
    u_total=29517/1000000.

Consequently the centroid coordinate is

    s_bar=u_total/m_total=9839/71650,

which lies strictly between 1/10 and 99/100. The closed halfspace
s>=s_bar contains the centroid and captures precisely the right interval,
with normalized mass

    m_right/m_total=133/1433 < 4/9=Gamma_2.                (9)

There is no boundary mass at this cap. Thus the ordinary Gamma_(d-1)
centroid theorem for each individual cell cannot be applied to their
actual geometric-group sum.

The failure has no positive universal centroid constant. Replace the
chosen a,b by a and a^2, let a decrease to zero, and use the analogous
chord. The total mass and first moment are

    m(a)=2a-a^2/2+2a^2-a^4/2,
    u(a)=a^2-a^3/3+2a^2-(3/2)a^4+a^6/3.

Thus s_bar(a)/a ->3/2, so the centroid lies in the gap
(a,1-a^2) for all sufficiently small a. The cap to its right has
fraction

    (2a^2-a^4/2)/m(a) ->0.                               (10)

All expressions are exact rational functions of a. This is an exact
family of geometric counterexamples to a group-centroid assertion
under the stated generic PL hypotheses, not numerical evidence.

## 4. The example obeys the relevant geometric compactness bounds

The inverse masses are uniformly bounded. Put u=t-delta_j H(s)>=0.
Since t<=u+2delta_j, integration in v and s gives the bound

    integral_(K_j) 1/L_j
       <= integral_0^1 (u+2delta_j)/(u+eta_j) du
       <=1+2delta_j log((1+eta_j)/eta_j)=O(1).              (11)

Changing the harmless upper integration endpoint from 1 to 1+eta_j
only weakens this estimate. The volumes M_j are bounded below.

Bulk logarithms are uniformly integrable. In the same coordinates,
the integral over {-log L_j>R} is bounded by a constant times

    integral_0^(exp(-R)) (u+2delta_j)(-log(u+eta_j))_+ du,

and enlarging the integrand to (u+2/3)(-log u) gives a bound tending
to zero as R tends to infinity.

The total positive logarithmic surface mass is bounded. The bottom
facet graph has area element

    delta_j A(s) sqrt(2+delta_j^2 A'(s)^2) ds dv.

On it -log L_j<=j, so its total positive log mass is O(1).
The faces x=0 and y=0 admit (s,t) coordinates with bounded area factor;
the substitution u=t-delta_j H(s)+eta_j bounds their log tails by
integrals of -log u near zero. The faces s=0 and s=1 have area element
t dt dv and the same bound with a factor t<=1. Their logarithms are
uniformly integrable. On the top face t=1 the logarithms tend uniformly
to zero. Edges have zero surface area.

On the bottom graph, at s in E one has L_j=eta_j and r_j=rho.
The product of -log L_j=j with its surface element converges to

    sqrt(2) H(s) ds dv.

For s outside E the product tends to zero: A-H is positive and the
logarithm grows only like log j at that fixed s. It is uniformly
bounded by the previous bottom estimate, so dominated convergence
applies. The outward normals tend to

    n=(0,-1,-1)/sqrt(2).

The actual positive-rate singular surface defect is therefore

    beta=sqrt(2)H(s)1_E(s)ds delta_n delta_rho.             (12)

For an interior anchor o with t_o=x_o+y_o>0, its limiting radial height
is h=(w-o) dot n=t_o/sqrt(2). The radially weighted defect is

    B=t_o H(s)1_E(s)ds delta_rho.

The limiting affine anchor value is b_o=t_o. Multiplying (8) by
M b_o=(1/2)t_o gives

    M b_o gamma_G(r)=t_o H(s)1_E(s)ds/rho

on 0<r<rho: exactly the uniform rate kernel generated by B at rho.
Thus the disconnected group law is compatible with the actual
geometric group-kernel identity and its exact constants.

## 5. No single ordinary uniform convex lift of this group

Let Q be a nonempty full-dimensional convex body in any finite
dimension, and let T be an affine map. The support of T_#(1_Q volume)
is exactly T(Q), a compact convex set: every relative neighborhood of
an image point meets the image of interior points and has positive
pushforward mass. In particular its support is connected.

The support of (8) is the disconnected set
[0,1/10] union [99/100,1] in the line F. Therefore (8) is not the
affine marginal of uniform volume on ANY one convex body, regardless
of the number of extra continuous variables.

Taking the convex hull of the two individual residual-density lifts
does not preserve the measure: it fills the gap and creates positive
projected mass there. Adding an integer cell label changes the integer
dimension and hence the target parity factor; it is not an unchanged
mixed-dimensional lift. This obstruction already occurs at n=0 and
inside a single physical fiber.

The source-count qualification in the introduction is essential here:
one cannot present this n=0 two-plane construction as an attained
canonical sampled-PL counterexample. A canonical obstruction would
also have to realize the planes at distinct integer source bases,
with the required source touching and projective-energy conditions.

The single-global-cell result in
candidate 185fb6155f830e0e
is unaffected: it treats each of the two cells separately, for which
the explicit affine densities do have the claimed convex lifts.

If instead lambda_j=rho/j^2, the same spatial inverse and surface
defects collapse to rate zero. Thus arbitrary zero-rate group defects
cannot be declared positively power-concave either. This retiming does
not address any additional variational condition selecting a particular
rate normalization in the OC proof framework.
